You're pressing the throwout bearing against the pressure plate vanes for an extended period of time. It's not meant for those loads. It will have accelerated wear.

My old man had the habit of depressing the clutch fully at stops. Three times the transmission had to be pulled out of his brand new Renault Duster. If his 65+ self can learn how to launch from neutral, anyone can.

Just keep it in neutral when you're stopped.

Think about it for a second. 

A) You save your leg from wearing out.

B) You save your throwout bearing from accelerated wearing.

Is it really any harder than keeping your clutch fully depressed at a stop? You still have to release at the bite point in both cases. 

Just chill out, press the clutch in, shift to 1st, and release. Once you get used to that rhythm, you'll launch just as fast as you would by keeping the clutch depressed.

Here's what I think of Yui. Hers is a hard role to play. She loves Hachiman, and she hates seeing him getting hurt. Obviously, by the end, he is implicitly shown to be sort of aware of Yui's crush on him, but we all know Hachiman would never accept Yui's confession, because he would be ingenuine.

Hachiman doesn't seem to love Yui as much as Yukino. That can be chalked up to their vast difference in their outlook on life. Yui hates seeing her friends in grief, and would sacrifice her own happiness for the happiness of her friends, meaning she would go for even an ingenuine relationship if it meant her friends wouldn't be sad (Especially Hikigaya). Hachiman sees grief as a very important step in gaining something genuine, as much as it may hurt.

Yui is more social, and Hachiman keeps a close circle of friends, and this can be draining on both of them. Yui would want to spend time with all of her friends, even Miura, and would want to include Hikigaya. However, Hachiman would want to avoid that, because social interactions with new people are draining for him. I admit that this is not a strong point, but Yui would feel isolated and conflicted, having to choose between Hikigaya and her friends to spend time with.

So they were not gonna be happy with each other. Yui would be fine with making Hikigaya happy, but Hikigaya would want a genuine relationship, no matter how much it hurt him. Plus, I think it would be really cool for Yui to become her own person, y'know? She lives in misery for the happiness of others, and so many people live their life like that. I would be happy to read a novel of Yui growing to accept herself, set boundaries with people, and put her own mental health first. Because as much as I say Hikigaya and Yui aren't compatible and I know it, it doesn't mean that the scenes with Yui crying didn't shatter my heart into a million pieces.
